experiments.scope: Exact recount of the structural counts of the trail search P (proof 2.1) for start lanes 0, 1. Trial 0 runs T1 (the depth-first search of in-kernel cores of at most 10 bits) from bit (lane, z = 0) of each lane of the group, counting every node, and for each core found whose smallest lane is in the group computes C1 (alpha4 compatible with beta3 = T2 leaves), decides P45 > 0 exactly (pruned search over the same alpha4), and, if P45 > 0, computes C2 (beta2 compatible with alpha3) and the number of half vectors of T3's meet-in-the-middle split (rows 0..h-1 and h..n-1 of alpha3, h minimising the sum of the two products). PASS iff the per-lane node counts and the group totals equal GROUP_LOG. The groups 0..3 (lanes 0-1, 2-7, 8-16, 17-24) partition the cores. Other trials return no pair. PASS = (00^135, 01||00^134) satisfies the declared event; FAIL = (00^135, 02||00^134) does not. Both are fixed sentinels, so the host check is vacuous; the evidence is the organizer's execution of the visible code, and the host-counted numbers are successes (PASS) and returned_pairs (PASS + FAIL).
experiments.hypothesis: P's structural counts that enter the time bound are exact. Predicted: PASS with 692,664 nodes, 1023 cores, sum C1 = 974,737,408, 204 cores with P45 > 0, sum C2 = 608,900,651,514, 21,466,134 half vectors. Over r5-trail-0..3: 8,674,833 nodes, 1741 cores, C1 = 1,639,088,128, 467 kept cores, C2 = 1,379,275,399,350 and 48,592,224 half vectors: the exact counts that P's charge multiplies by its prices (proof 2.1, 6).

experiments.scope: Counted programs (proof 2.1, 2.4, X, Y; W operators, load(), st() count 1, test() 2; 256-bit words) and P on small cases. EQS must be a basis of the equations of the 10 round-2 rows. Trials 0, 2, 4, 6 (E stage 1, X.4, Y.1): seeded basis, x of certificate r5-v6-000038's first message at a seeded inner slot p; fes_setup builds the degree-4 fast exhaustive search state over outer coordinates 0..8, then 511 counted fes_step calls (two unrolled blocks) walk the Gray order; PASS iff slot p passes at the start, all 24 residual bits and the pass bit equal e_plain at 3 slots of the start and 1 seeded slot after every step, every step counts exactly e_ops (25 + (1 if r == 0 else 2) per position from the block index + 2 max(0, dy - 1), + 24 x (2, 5, 8, 11) at even or (1, 3, 6, 9) at odd steps, less 14 or 28 at steps 3 mod 4) and each prologue at most 81. Trials 1, 3, 5, 7 (T2 leaf and Gray state step, X.2, Y.1): t2_leaf equals ALLOW on all 32 row values; then 64 leaves; PASS iff decisions and words equal a plain evaluation and counts <= 21. Trial 8: trail_search (core by core, W.4) with all 7 levels on the sub-problem [core 874, core 1136]; PASS iff no level certifies and the match count is 102 (native log). Trial 9: the same with the match cap at 0; PASS iff CapReached is raised. Trial 10: T3 at its certifying level (64 blocks) on the output core (core 17, re-derived by T1 from lane 0); PASS iff 49,060 matches (native log), 30 evaluations, least (w1, w2, choice) = (127, 24, 0.0.3.0.0.0.0.0.3.1) and beta2 = BETA2. Trial 11 (the E block price, X.4, Y.1): count-only fes_step on zero tables with 24 outer coordinates over the 256 steps of a seed-picked block index with at least four set bits, and the prologue for all 2^16 block indices; PASS iff the steps count exactly 66,418 and the largest prologue exactly 81 (block bound 66,499). Other trials: no pair. Sentinels and evidence as in r5-trail-0.
experiments.hypothesis: Prices of proof 6 and Y are counted longest paths (v24: E stage 1 at most 66,499 primitives per unrolled block of 256 steps, T2 leaf with its step <= 21), the counted stage 1 computes the plain round-2 predicate, and P's Python driver reproduces the native counts and stops at its cap; P's output trail is found at the level of 64 blocks with w1 = 127 <= 2 x 63 + 1, so the certification rule of proof 2.1 applies. Predicted: 12 PASS in 12 returned pairs.

experiments.scope: T3 of P at its certifying level of 64 blocks on one kept core picked by the organizer seed: q = SHA-256(seed || experiment id) mod 467; the core is re-derived by T1 from its smallest lane and the kept-core mask LANEM, checked to have P45 > 0, split into its two halves, and every block match is evaluated as in r5-count trial 10. PASS iff the match count equals the native per-core log MT6[q], and no evaluation is made (no leaf with AS <= 63) unless q is the output core, which must give the logged trail. Other trials: no pair. Sentinels as in r5-count. In production the seed is the organizer's; a holdout nonce changes the core.
experiments.hypothesis: Premise P (proof 2.1): the native T3 log, which gives every core's match and evaluation counts at each level, is the program's. Predicted: 1 PASS.

experiments.scope: T3 of P at its certifying level of 64 blocks on one kept core picked by the organizer seed: q = SHA-256(seed || experiment id) mod 467; the core is re-derived by T1 from its smallest lane and the kept-core mask LANEM, checked to have P45 > 0, split into its two halves, and every block match is evaluated as in r5-count trial 10. (v24, proof X.3, Y.1) Trial 1: the Gray state step with weight walks both full half tables of the output core (118,096 steps, every row reversing) updating 7 plane words and 14 key words (all 127 keys of the 7 levels: 63 keys of 26 bits in 7 words and 64 keys of 25 bits in 7 words); PASS iff at the first and every 4099th step the 21 words equal to_planes/keywords (v15's mkey) of halves()'s vector with the same choice vector, w2 equals halves()'s weight, and the longest step counts exactly 80. (v24, proof X.1, Y.1) Trial 2: on every level-64 match of the output core in up to 4 blocks picked by trial 0's seed, each a's run of matching B entries goes through match_run (per_a: A's 7 words, the counter with its M_CAP test and the dispatch of the 16-fold run loop; then the peel and the loop as executed control flow), and one seed-picked a goes against a run of 37 entries; PASS iff each run visits its entries once in order, AS and the decision equal the plain evaluation, the counter equals the matches and each run of e counts exactly 18 + 49 e + 3 floor(e/16). Other trials: no pair. Sentinels as in r5-count. In production the seed is the organizer's; a holdout nonce changes the core.
experiments.hypothesis: Premise P (proof 2.1): the native T3 log, which gives every core's match and evaluation counts at each level, is the program's. v24: the counted half-vector step (80, all keys and the entry pointer), per_a (18 per (a, block)) and match step (49 per match + 3 per 16 matches of a run) compute v15's vectors, keys, weights and decisions. Predicted: 3 PASS.

experiments.scope: The B' program bprime() with the R5 constants (no attempt limit per candidate, DMIN 33, D2u weights 1), its budget and its per-candidate cap, both enforced by the counter WK (proof 2.2), executed whole; then R7's count (v20) and the connector with organizer coins. Trial 0: the seed picks one of the R7 runs 6, 33, 37 (q = SHA-256(seed) mod 3; the three cheapest single-round R7 runs whose advice came from candidate 0, B' below 2^23.7 units, a rule fixed before R7's results), and B' runs from that run's label ('hashsmash sha3-256-r5 R7 run k') from candidate 0 to its output under the 2^32-unit budget and 2^26-unit CCAP; PASS iff (c, j, DF) and the advice hash equal RUNS[k], the whole-run cost counted by WK equals the R7 log (CHEAP[k], in 1/1355 units) and the facts of proof 3 hold. Trial 1: B' on R5 run 2's label ('hashsmash sha3-256-r5 R5 run 2') with a 2^22-unit budget and a 2^21-unit candidate cap; PASS iff candidate 0 is stopped by the candidate cap (candidate 1 starts after more than 2^21 and at most 2^21 + 2^13 units), exactly two candidates start, no advice is returned and the cost exceeds the budget by at most one counter update. Trial 2: PASS iff the table RUNS (v20: R7's) has 48 runs, 39 with an output (each with a status string of length i + 1), and the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound of 34 of 48 (exact binomial tail, bisection) is at least 0.40. Trials 3..26: one connector attempt on trial 0's advice with the trial's organizer seed as coins; PASS iff accepted and verify_space holds (Lemmas 1-2 at two random points). Other trials return no pair. Sentinels and evidence as in r5-trail-0. (v17) Trial 0 also reports the true cost of that B' run (WK's cost with Aff's table-update and copy sites at their word cost, proof V.5) as an observation. Rev-7: ladder prefix K=36, 34/48; fixed-design CP95 >=1.400*(0.40+0.0005), with allowance explicit; downstream selection remains heuristic.
experiments.hypothesis: Time bound and H1: B' stops each candidate at its cap and the run at its budget; the logged B' runs of R7 are the shipped program's runs; the success count of H1 is R7's table. (v17) The true cost of trial 0's B' run is below its WK cost. Predicted: PASS on trials 0-2 (trial 0 cost 16,446,246,658 or 13,220,514,578 or 11,331,166,259 for k = 6, 33, 37; trial 1: candidate 1 starts 0.68 units above 2^21, cost 2^22 + 188.1 units; trial 2: bound 0.582168); trials 3..26: descriptive acceptance (R7's label-seeded rate was 2400 of 6920 attempts). No bound uses this rate. Rev-7: ladder prefix K=36, 34/48; fixed-design CP95 >=1.400*(0.40+0.0005), with allowance explicit; downstream selection remains heuristic.

experiments.scope: Audit of the R7 study (proof W.2, Appendix F; v20), stratum 0 of 8: the R7 runs 1, 10, 19, 34, 42 (the 38 R7 runs with an output other than run 22 (our replay test measured a peak of 107.8 MB, too close to the sandbox's 128 MB; the collision is in R7's per-run ledger), in k order, stratum = position mod 8). Trial 0 picks run L[q0], q0 = SHA-256(trial 0 seed) mod n; trial 1 picks a different run, L[(q0 + 1 + SHA-256(trial 1 seed) mod (n - 1)) mod n]. For the picked run k (table RUNS: advice (c, j, DF, hash), first positive space idx, accepting attempt i, coordinate, DF of the space, status string of connector attempts 0..i): B' re-derives the advice from the label 'hashsmash sha3-256-r5 R7 run k' (candidate setup c, attempt j; accepted with the logged DF and advice hash; facts of proof 3); the status string must end with an accepted attempt, contain exactly idx accepted attempts and idx <= K = 36; the connector attempts i and min(i, 23) others drawn from 0..i-1 with the trial seed (all of 0..i if i < 24) are re-run with the run's coins (label || 'conn' || c + 1, attempt index) and must give the logged status of each; attempt i must be accepted with the logged DF; then the Python E (e_window) runs on the 2^12 aligned coordinates containing the logged coordinate. The trial returns E's first output if every check passes and the output is at the logged coordinate, otherwise no pair. Other trials return no pair. In production the seeds are the organizer's; a holdout nonce changes the picked runs and attempts.
experiments.hypothesis: H1 numerator: the successes in the R7 table are outputs of v20's algorithm (B', connector rule, E) run from their labels, at the logged place among the advice's 50 accepted spaces. Predicted: 2 full 5-round collisions of distinct 135-byte messages.
